docs.title: Fleet & Road Realism
docs.text:
Fleet & Road Realism is a plugin (DLL) with mod for Euro Truck Simulator 2 by Ventyres 3D. It makes fleet, registration, jobs, cargo and vehicles more realistic: real number plates of all countries, registration with insurance and vehicle tax, securing cargo by hand, partial loads and tour planning, driving bans, load-sensing brakes, mirror and windscreen features and much more.

Fleet & Road Realism is free, based on voluntary donations.

  • For players

    What the mod does in the game and what every setting does.

    Features · Settings

  • For modders

    Optional .v3def files that let truck, trailer, cargo and map mods set everything themselves.

    Modding resources

News and info: Facebook – Ventyres 3D

docs.title: Modding resources
docs.text:
Fleet & Road Realism reads small, optional .v3def files next to the files the game already loads. This lets truck, trailer, cargo and map mods set everything the game files do not contain. A missing file or line means the default applies – that is not an error. An existing line with a wrong format is logged as an error in game.log and in fleet_road_realism.log.

Fleet & Road Realism does not ship ready-made v3defs for other mods – these resources let everyone build their own.

Area Download Vehicle data resources_vehicle_data.zip Cargo data resources_cargo_data.zip Company and container data resources_company_data.zip Truck driving bans resources_driving_ban.zip Cargo securing resources_lashing_data.zip

Everything in one package: fleet_road_realism_resources.zip

docs.title: Truck driving bans
docs.text: Driving bans, exemptions and fines live in small .v3def files next to the files the game already loads: per country, per city and per cargo. Map and cargo mods can bring their own countries, cities and cargo this way. The examples in the def/ folder of this package show the format.

docs.title: 1. Where the files go
docs.text:
Country: /def/country/<country>.v3def   (<country> = country token, e.g. germany)
City:    /def/city/<city>.v3def         (<city> = city token, e.g. warszawa)
Cargo:   /def/cargo/<cargo>.v3def       (<cargo> = cargo token)

If a country .v3def already holds entries (e.g. driver_wage), simply add the blocks below them. A missing file means no ban there - that is not an error. A line with a wrong format is logged as an error (file, line, value read) and is not used.

docs.title: 2. Ban blocks
docs.text:
Three kinds, each may appear more than once:

driving_banapplies to all trucks driving_ban_adrdangerous goods only (cargo with an ADR class) driving_ban_oversizespecial transports only (heavy haulage jobs)

Same layout as the companies' opening hours: one day per line, one or more time windows (hh.mm, hh.mm). A missing day has no ban. A ban across midnight is split over both days (saturday until 24.00, sunday from 00.00). Days: monday tuesday wednesday thursday friday saturday sunday

Extra lines in the block (all optional):

transit: trueapplies to through traffic only. Loading or unloading in the country / city (sender or target of the job) is free, so is driving out after unloading and to your own garage there. inbound: trueapplies only if the city is the job's target to: <country>applies only if the job's target country matches rural: trueapplies only outside cities tractor_solo: truea tractor without trailer is free min_cargo: 1500applies only from this cargo mass in kg share: 50an exemption only counts if the exempt cargo makes up at least this percentage of the load (mixed loads) combined: 150combined transport: a container chassis with a company that has a reach stacker (container_load: true) as sender or target is free up to this distance (km straight line) 
Exempt cargo categories as their own block, one entry per line:
  exempt :
  {
  milk
  meat
  }

Fine as its own block inside the ban block:
  fine :
  {
  driver: 250 750       driver's share in EUR; several values = 1st, 2nd offence
  holder: 3750          holder's share in EUR (own truck), tiered the same way
  by_time: true         optional: values follow the time driven during the ban
                        (up to 1 h, up to 2 h, above) instead of the offence
  }
One value applies to every offence. If a city's ban block has no fine block,
the country's fine block of the same kind (driving_ban, _adr, _oversize)
applies. In a driver job you only pay the driver's share, with your own truck
both shares.

City blocks replace the country blocks of the same kind for that city.

docs.text:
One line per category:
  ban_class[]: milk
  ban_class[]: perishable

Categories:
  perishable     perishable food in general
  milk           milk and dairy products
  meat           meat and meat products
  fish           fish and fish products
  fruit_veg      fruit and vegetables
  bakery         fresh bakery products
  livestock      live animals
  flowers        cut flowers and plants
  post           mail and press
  medical        medicine and hospital supplies
  fuel           fuel for filling stations
  gas_supply     heating and medical gas

  removal        household removals
  animal_byprod  animal by-products
Milk, meat, fish, fruit/vegetables and bakery products also get perishable,
because some countries only name "perishable food".
Empty runs to a reserved / booked exempt cargo and after unloading an exempt
cargo are free.

docs.title: Vehicle data
docs.text:
Taxes and road charges of the own registration (vehicle tax in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, France, Italy, Poland, Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary, Greece, Romania, Bulgaria, Slovenia, Croatia, Serbia, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Albania, Turkey, Russia, Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia and Kosovo, Swiss LSVA) need data about a vehicle. Most of it is read from the vehicle's own .sii files:

engine .siipower (info[] "... (270@@kw@@)", otherwise from torque and torque_curve[]), displacement (volume), electric (type: electric) chassis .siinumber of axles (residual_travel[]), empty weight (truck: sum of kerb_weight[], trailer: trailer_mass) body .siimass (added to trailer_mass)

What the game files do not contain (Euro class, permissible weights, tractor or rigid truck, kind of suspension) comes from small optional files that a truck or trailer mod can ship next to its own definitions. The same files also set the position of plates and signs, doubles (registration, splitting when loading, cables, coupling sounds, coupling guide, support legs), animated accessories, the deck and the trailer lengths of driver tours.

All files are optional. A missing file or a missing line is not an error, the default value given for each entry under "Keys" is used.

docs.title: Where the files go
docs.text:
Same folder and same name as the .sii the vehicle uses, only with .v3def:

engine         /def/vehicle/truck/your_truck/engine/your_engine.sii
            -> /def/vehicle/truck/your_truck/engine/your_engine.v3def

truck chassis  /def/vehicle/truck/your_truck/chassis/your_chassis.sii
            -> /def/vehicle/truck/your_truck/chassis/your_chassis.v3def

trailer        /def/vehicle/trailer_owned/your_trailer/chassis/your_chassis.sii
            -> /def/vehicle/trailer_owned/your_trailer/chassis/your_chassis.v3def

company trailer (job trailer, no chassis/ folder: the chassis is the .sii
whose name starts with "chassis")
               /def/vehicle/trailer/your_company_trailer/chassis_hook.sii
            -> /def/vehicle/trailer/your_company_trailer/chassis_hook.v3def

accessory      /def/vehicle/trailer_owned/your_trailer/accessory/r_bumper/your_bumper.sii
            -> /def/vehicle/trailer_owned/your_trailer/accessory/r_bumper/your_bumper.v3def
               (rear bumpers, see "ACCESSORY REAR BUMPER" under "Keys")

mirror         /def/vehicle/truck/your_truck/accessory/mirror/your_mirror.sii
            -> /def/vehicle/truck/your_truck/accessory/mirror/your_mirror.v3def
               (also s_mirror, f_mirror etc., see "ACCESSORY MIRROR" under "Keys")

interior       /def/vehicle/truck/your_truck/interior/your_interior.sii
            -> /def/vehicle/truck/your_truck/interior/your_interior.v3def
               (sleeping, windshield curvature, see "ACCESSORY INTERIOR")

cabin          /def/vehicle/truck/your_truck/cabin/your_cabin.sii
            -> /def/vehicle/truck/your_truck/cabin/your_cabin.v3def
               (washer nozzles, see "WASHER NOZZLES")

The examples in the def/ folder of this package show the format.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
key: value
  • one entry per line, spaces or tabs around the colon are allowed
  • lines starting with # or // are comments, a # after the value too
  • weights: tonnes (values up to 100, e.g. 18.00) or kilograms (above 100, e.g. 18000)
  • decimal point or decimal comma (18.50 or 18,50), no thousands separator
  • emission: whole number 0-7
  • type: tractor or rigid
  • suspension: air or leaf
  • registration: own, next or prev
  • loading: own, next or prev
  • load_split: true or false
  • fixed_plate: game token of the country, e.g. germany, optionally |code
  • cylinders: whole number 1-16
  • knock_strength: number 0-3 (e.g. 0.5)
  • knock_tone: number 0.4-2 (e.g. 0.7)
  • mirror_axes: horizontal, vertical or both
  • mirror_rain_size: number above 0 up to 20 (e.g. 0.5)
  • sleeper: true or false
  • bed_head: a or b
  • washer: fixed or wiper
  • washer_jets: single or double
  • washer_jets_angle: degrees 5-170
  • coordinates (bed_area, washer_spot[], washer[n]): x;y;z as ZModeler shows them
  • italy_/serbia_card_shift_front / _rear: millimetres, positive = up, negative = down, -200 to 200 (e.g. 15 or -7.5)
  • italy_/serbia_card_depth_front / _rear: millimetres, positive = away from the vehicle, negative = towards the vehicle, -200 to 200
  • italy_/serbia_card_tilt_rear: degrees, positive = top edge towards the vehicle, negative = top edge away from the vehicle, -45 to 45 (e.g. 12.5)
  • greece_export_shift_front / _rear: millimetres, positive = up, negative = down, -200 to 200
  • greece_export_depth_front / _rear: millimetres, positive = away from the vehicle, negative = towards the vehicle, -200 to 200
  • greece_export_rotate_front / _rear: degrees, positive = top edge towards the vehicle, negative = top edge away from the vehicle, -45 to 45
  • plate_depth_front / _rear: millimetres, positive = away from the vehicle, negative = towards the vehicle, -200 to 200
  • plate_rotate_front / _rear: degrees, positive = top edge towards the vehicle, negative = top edge away from the vehicle, -45 to 45
  • nothing else on the line (no units like "t" or "kg")

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Every entry starts with >>> and shows the line as it goes into the v3def (<...> = your value, | = one of them). Everything below it is description.

docs.title: ENGINE
docs.text: /def/vehicle/truck/xxxx/engine/xxxx.v3def

docs.title: emission: 0 - 7
docs.text:
Euro class 0-7

Default: Euro 6

COLD START KNOCK

A cold diesel knocks: the mod adds a short metallic knock per ignition to the engine sound of the own truck, plus slightly uneven running and a harsher sound. How cold the engine is comes from the oil temperature exactly as the game computes it for cold_start_rpm (full up to about 19 deg C, gone from 90 deg C). Strongest at idle and when pulling away under load at low rpm, weaker with rising rpm. Electric engines do not knock. The engine sound comes from sounds[] "engine|..." of the engine .sii (also through @include), directly as "<bank>#<event>" or through a .soundref. Only this event gets the knock, not exhaust, turbo etc. Nothing has to be entered for it; the three lines below are only fine tuning.

docs.title: cylinders: <1 - 16>
docs.text:
number of cylinders; sets the rate of the knocks (rpm / 60 x cylinders / 2 per second)

Default: 6

docs.title: knock_strength: <0 - 3>
docs.text:
strength of the knock (and of the uneven running) for this engine, 1 = normal, 0.5 = half as strong, 2 = double, 0 = off

Default: 1

docs.title: knock_tone: <0.4 - 2>
docs.text:
pitch of the knock for this engine, so it matches the engine sound; lower = deeper and duller (e.g. big V8), higher = brighter and harder

Default: 1

docs.title: TRUCK CHASSIS
docs.text: /def/vehicle/truck/xxxx/chassis/xxxx.v3def

docs.title: type: tractor | rigid
docs.text:
tractor = tractor unit for semi-trailers rigid = rigid truck (load on its own frame)

Default: tractor

docs.title: fixed_plate: "<country>" | "<country>|<code>"
docs.text:
plates fixed in the model (without the game's plate locator), e.g. for packs with real, fixed plates on the vehicle

fixed_plate: "germany"
fixed_plate: "germany|HN"

The vehicle is permanently registered in this country from the purchase:
no temporary plate, no registration duty. Vehicle tax by the rules of
this country (weight, axles, Euro class etc. from the other entries, as
for any vehicle). Insurance is the statutory liability insurance,
changeable in the insurance menu (F7). The registration service is locked
for the vehicle: no registration tile in the service shop, no click on
the plate in the manager.
<country> = game token of the country (germany, austria, netherlands ...).
<code> = registration district as shown in the registration window;
without code the default district of the country. Matters where the tax
depends on the district (e.g. Poland, Romania, France).
Vehicles already owned (temporary, deregistered or registered in another
country) are re-registered to the country once; the old tax ends, no-claims
class and insurance stay.
Default:  no entry = normal registration

docs.title: gross_combination_weight: <tonnes or kg>
docs.text:
permissible gross combination weight

Default: 40 t

docs.title: plate_depth_front: <mm>
docs.text:
front plate forward/back, mm

Works like the cardboard keys, but for all normal plates of the chassis
(permanent and temporary plates; the cardboard signs and papers keep their own
keys). plate_depth_front / plate_depth_rear move the plate forward or back in
millimetres: positive values away from the vehicle (e.g. out of a recess or a
bumper), negative values towards the vehicle. plate_rotate_front /
plate_rotate_rear tilt the plate around its horizontal centre line (seen from
the side), in degrees: positive values move the top edge towards the vehicle
and the bottom edge away from it, negative values the other way round. A
trailer only has the rear plate. Only the vehicles of your company are moved.

  plate_depth_rear: 12        # rear plate 12 mm further out
  plate_rotate_front: -8      # front plate, top edge tilted 8 degrees away
Default:  0

docs.title: plate_rotate_front: <degrees>
docs.text:
front plate tilt, degrees

Default: 0

docs.title: italy_card_shift_front: <mm>
docs.text:
Italian cardboard plate (foglio di via) front up/down, mm

The Italian temporary registration (foglio di via, cardboard 275 x 200 mm) and the Serbian test plate (PROBA, cardboard 340 x 180 mm) are cardboard signs that are much larger than a plate. Depending on the model they can reach up to a rear light, be hidden behind an underrun guard or disappear into the plate recess. Italy uses the italy_card_ keys, Serbia the serbia_card_ keys. The Montenegrin test plate (PROBA) has the same size as the Serbian one and also uses the serbia_card_* keys, so one setting fits both.

The default height already fits the vehicles of the game:

truck frontcentred on the plate truck rear30 mm lower than the plate trailer10 mm lower than the plate

..._card_shift_front / ..._card_shift_rear move the sign up or down from this default for one chassis, in millimetres: positive values up, negative values down. ..._card_depth_front / ..._card_depth_rear move it forward or back: positive values away from the vehicle (out of the plate recess), negative values towards the vehicle. ..._card_tilt_rear tilts the rear sign around its horizontal centre line (seen from the side), in degrees: positive values move the top edge towards the vehicle and the bottom edge away from it (e.g. to follow an inclined plate holder), negative values the other way round. A trailer only has the rear sign.

  italy_card_shift_rear: 15      # 15 mm higher than the default
  italy_card_shift_front: -10    # 10 mm lower than the default
  serbia_card_depth_rear: 20     # 20 mm further out of the plate recess
  serbia_card_tilt_rear: 10      # top edge tilted 10 degrees towards the vehicle
Default:  0

docs.text:
Italian cardboard plate front forward/back, mm

Default: 0

docs.title: serbia_card_shift_front: <mm>
docs.text:
Serbian/Montenegrin cardboard plate (PROBA) front up/down, mm

Default: 0

docs.title: serbia_card_depth_front: <mm>

Default: 0

docs.title: greece_export_shift_front: <mm>
docs.text:
Greek export plate front up/down, mm

The Greek export plate is smaller and higher than a normal plate (370 x 120 mm instead of 520 x 110 mm) and is drawn as a plate of its own, centred on the normal plate. greece_export_shift_front / _rear move it up or down in millimetres (positive up), greece_export_depth_front / _rear forward or back (positive away from the vehicle), greece_export_rotate_front / _rear tilt it around its horizontal centre line in degrees (positive = top edge towards the vehicle). Without an entry all values are 0. A trailer only has the rear plate.

  greece_export_shift_rear: 12     # 12 mm higher
  greece_export_rotate_front: -5   # top edge tilted 5 degrees away
Default:  0

docs.title: greece_export_depth_front: <mm>
docs.text:
Greek export plate front forward/back, mm

Default: 0

docs.title: greece_export_rotate_front: <degrees>
docs.text:
Greek export plate front tilt, degrees

Default: 0

TILTING FIFTH WHEEL

The fifth wheel plate can tilt around its bearing. When coupled it follows the longitudinal tilt of the trailer relative to the truck, also while driving under a trailer front, otherwise it falls back to its rest position. A sound plays when it hits the trailer and when it falls back, louder or quieter depending on the force. The plate is a model of its own at a locator of the chassis model:

couple_model: "/vehicle/truck/your_truck/fifthwheel.pmd"
couple_tilt_front: 10
couple_tilt_rear: 15
couple_tilt_rest: 5
  • locator couple_0 in the chassis model = bearing of the plate (with several fifth wheels couple_1, couple_2 ... with [1], [2] ... on the keys)
  • the plate (.pmd): only the tilting part, origin in the bearing, orientation as in the truck. The chassis model itself no longer contains the plate (in the coarser LODs it may stay fixed)

docs.text: model of the tilting plate at locator couple_n; without [n] = [0]

Default: rigid (no forward tilt)

Default: rigid (no backward tilt)

Default: from the centre of mass of the plate

docs.title: couple_contact_sound[n]: <.soundref or .bank#event, - = no sound>
docs.text:
sound when the plate hits the trailer

Default: sound of the mod (/sound/lphd/fifthwheel.bank#contact)

docs.text:
/def/vehicle/trailer_owned/xxxx/chassis/xxxx.v3def
company trailer: /def/vehicle/trailer/xxxx/chassis_xxxx.v3def

docs.title: king_pin_load: <tonnes or kg>
docs.text:
load on the king pin (semi-trailers only; without it the trailer counts as a drawbar trailer)

Default: by number of axles: 1 -> 10 t, otherwise 12 t (only together with the default gross weight)

docs.title: registration: own | next | prev
docs.text:
own = own registration next = belongs to the part behind it prev = belongs to the part in front of it

Owned trailers with more than one chassis (B-double, HCT, semi-trailer on a converter dolly, full trailer with turntable) are a chain of parts in the game. Without a "registration" line every part is a vehicle of its own: own entry in the registration office, own plate, own tax and insurance. That is correct for semi-trailers and for converter dollies, which are registered vehicles of their own in reality.

"registration: next" or "registration: prev" joins a chassis with its neighbour. Use it only for parts that are not a vehicle of their own in reality, e.g. the turntable axle (front part) of a full trailer with turntable steering. Joined parts are one vehicle:

  • one entry in the registration office, registered under the plate of the rearmost part (the one seen at the rear)
  • tax and insurance once, for the whole vehicle
  • no temporary plate of its own when bought; the joined part keeps the plate the game gives it

"next" and "prev" are relative to the position, so the same chassis works in every configuration it is used in. Joins can be chained.

Values of a joined vehicle
  axles          sum of the parts
  empty weight   sum of the parts
  gross weight   sum of gross_vehicle_weight of all parts
                 minus king_pin_load of every part behind the first one
                 (that load rests on the part in front of it and is already
                 counted there)
  king pin load  the one of the front part (load on the truck)

Give every part the values it has on its own - nothing has to be split.

Example 1: full trailer with turntable, 2 axles, 18 t (one vehicle)

turntable axle (front)   registration: next
                         gross_vehicle_weight: 9.00
                         (no king_pin_load = drawbar, nothing on the truck)
rear part                gross_vehicle_weight: 9.00
                         (no king_pin_load)

-> 1 vehicle, 2 axles, 9 + 9 = 18 t, no king pin load on the truck

The same result with the rear part carried by the turntable:
rear part gross_vehicle_weight: 18.00 and king_pin_load: 9.00
-> 9 + 18 - 9 = 18 t

Example 2: semi-trailer on a converter dolly (two vehicles, no "registration" line)

converter dolly          gross_vehicle_weight: 18.00
                         (no king_pin_load = drawbar)
semi-trailer             gross_vehicle_weight: 39.00
                         king_pin_load: 12.00

-> 2 vehicles with 2 registrations, each taxed with its own values
   (dolly 18 t, semi-trailer 39 t with 12 t on the dolly)

Example 3: HCT semi-trailer + converter dolly + semi-trailer

no "registration" lines -> 3 vehicles (semi-trailer, dolly, semi-trailer)

"prev" on the first part or "next" on the last part of a trailer is an error (see below), the part then counts as "own". Default: own

docs.title: loading: own | next | prev
docs.text:
With the option "Split own doubles when loading" the chain of a trailer is spread over several loading lanes of the company: from the rear, every part gets a lane of its own and is detached there (key for detaching), the front part stays on the truck and is loaded on the lane of the game. After loading, the parts are coupled back together; the tour starts when the chain is complete. When unloading, the chain is only split if the hardest choice (most XP) is taken in the trailer delivery window.

This works for own trailers and for company (job) trailers alike. It is only done when cargo is loaded or unloaded: simply dropping the trailer with the key for detaching (e.g. at a workshop or a trailer hub) always keeps the chain together.

Which links belong together is set with "loading" in the v3def of every chassis
of the chain:
  own   the link is a loading unit of its own
  next  the link stays with the link behind it (e.g. a converter dolly stays
        under the rear semi-trailer)
  prev  the link stays with the link in front of it

If one link of the chain has no "loading" line, or a line that cannot be read, the chain is never split.

The line is only read for the chain the trailer is in at the moment. A trailer with "loading: own" that runs as a single trailer is loaded as usual; the same trailer can be the front part of a double or stand behind a dolly with "next" in another chain.

front semi-trailerfront_trailer.v3def loading: own converter dollydolly.v3def loading: next rear semi-trailerrear_trailer.v3def loading: own 
-> 2 parts: front semi-trailer / dolly + rear semi-trailer

Example: company (job) double, semi-trailer + centre-axle trailer (files in def/vehicle/trailer/your_company_trailer/)

front semi-trailerchassis_hook.v3def loading: own centre-axle trailerchassis_ca.v3def loading: own 
  -> 2 parts: semi-trailer / centre-axle trailer
Default:  none (the chain is never split)

docs.title: cable: prev | next | both | none
docs.text:
who keeps the cable strand when split: prev, next, both or none

When the chain of an own double is split (option "Split own doubles when loading", or a part detached with the key for detaching), the game itself has no rule for the cable strand between the two parts. The chassis .v3def decides:

cable: prevthis part keeps the strand to the part in front of it cable: nextthis part keeps the strand to the part behind it cable: bothprev and next cable: nonethis part never keeps a strand

Several "cable" lines are allowed. Between the front part A and the rear part B:

1. B has prev or both-> the strand stays at B (rest position at B) 2. otherwise A has next or both-> the strand stays at A (rest position as in the game) 3. otherwise A has none-> the strand stays at B 4. otherwise-> the strand is removed

A strand that stays at the rear part keeps its trailer plug in the socket (e.g. of the dolly); the free end goes to a rest point of the chassis model:

cable_rest_prev {
    rst_cable_y : 0.45; 1.20; 5.80 : 0; 0; 0
    rst_cable_w : 0.55; 1.20; 5.80 : 0; 0; 0
}
name : x; y; z : heading; pitch; roll(metres, degrees, chassis model)

The entry is chosen by the rest name of the cable accessory (upper / lower case does not matter); if the accessory has no rest name, by the ending of the socket locator (ele_cable_w -> ..._w), otherwise by the order of the strands. Missing rest points are listed in fleet_road_realism.log. When the parts are coupled again, the game cables the chain as usual and the rest strands disappear.

How the DLL lays a rest strand:

  • The Z axis of the rest point (and of the socket locator) points to the end of the cable, i.e. to the plug head. The cable leaves on the opposite side: if the rest point points down, the cable goes up out of the plug.
  • Length: for straight cables straight_cable_length of the cable accessory, otherwise the rope length of the game.
  • At both ends the cable makes a bend (stiffness, the longer the cable, the wider); the extra length sags down in the middle.
  • The cable lies on the boxes of the chassis collision (.pmc, or collision_override): on a drawbar it lies on top. Boxes above both cable ends (frame, body) push the cable to the side or down, never over them.
  • If the cable is shorter than the way from the socket to the rest point, it is drawn taut - then move the rest point closer to the socket.

Default: none (when split, the cable strand between the parts is removed)

ds   driver side wide angle (cam_ds)      ps   passenger side wide angle (cam_ps)

Driver and passenger side also apply to right-hand drive (UK models).

  • Exterior glasses are drawn on every vehicle with this mirror; only the own truck is adjusted, all others stay neutral.

docs.title: What the values are used for
docs.text:
Germany (own registration)vehicle tax by emission class Austria (own registration)vehicle tax per started tonne and month: up to 12 t 1.55 EUR (min. 15), 12-18 t 1.70 EUR, above 18 t 1.90 EUR; max. 80 EUR truck, 66 EUR trailer trailer weight = gross_vehicle_weight - king_pin_load

Switzerland (own registration) cantonal vehicle tax, tariff of the canton on the plate, per calendar year in advance (pro rata in the year of registration, rest refunded when the vehicle is sold, deregistered or moved to another canton). Depending on the canton by gross weight, payload (gross weight - empty weight), gross combination weight (tractor units), displacement or power; some cantons use the Euro class or reduce the tax for electric trucks. The number stays reserved for the company for one year after a sale.

Switzerland (all trucks)LSVA = km in Switzerland x weight x tariff weight = truck + coupled trailer - king_pin_load, max. 40 t; tariff by emission (Rappen per tkm): Euro 0-3 3.26, Euro 4-5 2.82, Euro 6-7 2.39 electric trucks (engine "type: electric") are exempt France (own registration)TSVR (heavy vehicle tax), settled in arrears per calendar year from a logbook (day by day): rigid trucks from 12 t by axles and gross weight, tractor units by gross combination weight and the axles of the trailer pulled that day (no trailer: nothing); air / other suspension Italy (own registration)IPT at registration: tractor units by power (kW), rigid trucks and trailers by payload (gross weight - empty weight); bollo per year: rigid trucks by axles, gross weight and suspension, tractor units by region and axles (2 / 3 or more) Poland (own registration)tax on means of transport (two instalments a year): rigid trucks by axles and gross weight, tractor units by axles and gross combination weight, trailers by axles; air / other suspension; rates of the municipality (minimum rates otherwise) Czechia (own registration)road tax for trucks from 12 t, in arrears per calendar year (1/12 per started month): rigid trucks by axles and gross weight, tractor units by axles and gross combination weight (trailers are covered by the tractor); air / other suspension Slovakia (own registration)motor vehicle tax, in arrears per calendar year (1/12 per month, return by 31 January, prepayments quarterly above 700 EUR / monthly above 8,300 EUR of the previous year's tax): rigid trucks by axles and gross weight, tractor units by axles and gross combination weight, air / other suspension; trailers (O4) a flat 150 EUR; trucks pay an age surcharge (+10 % after 3 years, rising every 3 years, +50 % from the 181st month) counted from the first registration in the game Hungary (own registration)motor vehicle tax per started 100 kg, paid by 15 April for the months up to the end of the year (from the month after registration to the month of deregistration): rigid trucks and trailers empty weight + 50 % of the payload, tractor units 2 x empty weight + 1/2 x (gross combination weight - 2 x empty weight); air / other suspension; reductions for Euro III (-20 %, tractor units -30 %) and Euro IV-V (-30 % / -50 %), none for Euro I-II and Euro VI; electric trucks (class 5E, emission entry ignored) -20 % / -30 %. Acquisition duty at the first registration in Hungary: trucks per kW by power and age (from the first registration in the game), trailers flat 24,000 Ft Greece (own registration)road tax per calendar year in advance (full year with the registration, then on 1 November for the following year): rigid trucks by gross weight (up to 10 t 300 EUR, 20 t 600, 30 t 940, 40 t 1,320, above 1,490), tractor units 300 EUR, trailers free. Used trucks below Euro V (emission 0-4) cannot be registered in Greece; electric trucks are exempt from this rule. Romania (own registration)tax on means of transport per calendar year: rigid trucks by axles and gross weight, tractor units by their axles + the axles of the semi-trailer chosen at registration (none coupled: 3) and gross combination weight; air / other suspension. The tractor pays for the combination, the semi-trailer pays nothing. Electric trucks use the same table. The owner on 31 December pays for the next year: registered during the year -> from 1 January of the following year; whole year on 31 March with a bonus (10 %, Bacau 5 %); surcharge of the town of the garage (Brasov +35 %, Craiova +13 %, Timisoara +50 %); no refund on sale/deregistration Bulgaria (own registration)vehicle tax per year: rigid trucks by axles and gross weight, tractor units by axles and gross combination weight; air / other suspension; multiple of the minimum rate set by the town of the garage (otherwise by the plate code): Sofia 1.25, Plovdiv 1.43, Varna 2.25, Burgas 1.5, Veliko Tarnovo 1.3, Stara Zagora 1.5, others 1.0; Euro 4 -20 %, Euro 5-6 -50 % (not in Stara Zagora, electric trucks full rate); trailers no own tax. Whole year by 30 April with 5 % discount; in the year of registration 1/12 per month from the month of registration (due in two months); sale or deregistration: tax up to the end of the month, overpaid tax refunded Slovenia (own registration)annual vehicle charge = days x daily rate, one year in advance with the registration, then yearly: rigid trucks per started tonne of gross weight, tractor units per kW up to 190 kW (above a flat daily rate), separate rates up to / above 20 t gross weight; trailers per tonne of gross weight, semi-trailers free. Euro VI -35 %, V -25 %, IV 0, III +10 %, II +20 %, I +30 %, 0 +40 %; electric trucks -90 %; air suspension (rigid trucks only) a further -15 %. Minimum 5 EUR; rest refunded on sale/deregistration (amounts up to 5 EUR not) Croatia (own registration)road charge 40 EUR x coefficient, one year in advance with the registration: trucks by gross weight and axles, trailers by gross weight and axles, semi-trailers by the sum of the axle loads (gross_vehicle_weight - king_pin_load). Environment charge (trucks only): 60.52 EUR x displacement factor x age factor (age from the first registration in the game); electric trucks 0. No refund on sale/deregistration Serbia (own registration)municipal fee per year (due at registration, then yearly, maximum rates for all areas): rigid trucks and trailers by payload (gross weight - empty weight), tractor units by power (kW); no refund on sale/deregistration Montenegro (own registration)road charge for 12 months in advance with the registration, then with each renewal (shorter registration pro rata by months); no refund, a new owner pays nothing until it expires. Until 30 June 2027: rigid trucks and trailers by payload (gross weight - empty weight), tractor units by power (kW); from 1 July 2027: 5 EUR x coefficient by gross weight and axles (separate tables for trailers and semi-trailers). Short-term liability insurance: rigid trucks and trailers by payload, tractor units by power (kW) North Macedonia (own registration)road fee for 12 months with the registration (shorter registration pro rata, 30 days = 1 month), no refund: tractor units by power (kW), rigid trucks and trailers by payload (gross weight - empty weight), semi-trailers flat 5,200 MKD Bosnia and Herzegovina (own registration)annual charges for 12 months in advance with the registration, by the entity of the district. Federation: road charge 30 KM x coefficient, trucks and tractor units by gross weight and axles, semi-trailers by the sum of the axle loads (gross_vehicle_weight - king_pin_load), trailers by gross weight; environment charge (trucks only) by fuel (electric x 0.2), displacement and age (from the first registration in the game); water charge 0.30 KM per kW (not electric trucks); road charge refunded from the day of deregistration. Republika Srpska: road toll by gross weight, tractor units flat 120 KM; no refund Albania (own registration)TVMP (trucks only): displacement x age coefficient x 12.5 ALL; free in the first 3 years, 0.20 in the 4th year, +0.02 per year up to 0.60 (age from the first registration in the game); electric trucks and trailers pay nothing. Valid 365 days from payment, no refund; after a temporary deregistration pro rata per month to 31 December Turkey (own registration)MTV (trucks only, trailers free) by gross weight of the truck (not the combination) and age (1-6, 7-15, 16+ years, counted from the year of the first registration in the game); two equal instalments in January and July, with the registration the instalment of the current half-year; after sale/deregistration no further instalments Russia (own registration)transport tax (trucks only, trailers free): horsepower (kW x 1.35962) x rate of the region on the plate (in some regions by age from the first registration in the game) x months / 12; paid in arrears per quarter (28 April, 28 July, 28 October, 1 March); a month counts when registered by the 15th / deregistered after the 15th; no refund, open months after deregistration are charged on the next date Lithuania (own registration)annual charge from 12 t gross weight (trucks and trailers), by tonne of gross weight (semi-trailers: gross_vehicle_weight - king_pin_load), air / other suspension; 12 months with the registration, then yearly; no refund Latvia (own registration)vehicle operation tax per calendar year: trucks up to 12 t by Euro class, above 12 t by axles and Euro class (own table for tractor units); electric trucks free. Trailers above 3.5 t: one axle 66 EUR, otherwise by axles, suspension of the towing vehicle and weight (semi-trailer: empty weight of the tractor + gross weight of the semi-trailer; trailer: gross weight of truck + trailer); the towing vehicle is chosen at registration (default: tractor 2 axles, 7.7 t empty, air suspension / rigid truck 3 axles, 26 t). With the registration the remaining months including the current one, then every January; deregistration: full remaining months refunded Estonia (own registration)heavy vehicle tax per quarter: rigid trucks from 12 t by axles, gross weight and suspension (air / other); tractor units as a combination: own axles + axles of the semi-trailer chosen at registration (default 3), by gross combination weight; trailers free. With the registration the full remaining months of the quarter (without the registration month), then the whole quarter on 1 January / April / July / October; no refund, after deregistration nothing from the next quarter Kosovo (own registration)road tax 90 EUR + eco tax 30 EUR for 365 days with the registration (trucks and trailers, flat, no vehicle values); renewal 170 EUR (incl. 50 EUR administration); no refund

# Fleet & Road Realism - Beispiel: hinterer Teil eines Doubles (Sattelauflieger, der allein stehen kann)

# See README, keys "cable", "dbl_coupling", "model_override" and "trailer_brace_up_sound"

# eigene Ladeeinheit, behaelt den Kabelstrang zum Teil davor
# loading unit of its own, keeps the cable strand to the part in front

cable: prev

# Ruhepunkt fuer das freie Steckerende (Name wie der Ruhe-Name des Kabel-Zubehoers);
# die Z-Achse zeigt zum Steckerkopf - hier nach unten, das Kabel geht nach oben heraus
# rest point for the free plug end (name as the rest name of the cable accessory);

cable_rest_prev {
    rst_cable : 0.117;0.616;-3.525 : -59.77;90;90
}

# Fanghilfe vorne (Zugoese / Koenigszapfen), Werte wie ZModeler sie anzeigt

  cylinder : 0;0.539275;-5.769051 : 90.036583;0;0 : 0.053878;0.033937
  box : 0;0.539275;-5.651069 : 90.036583;0;0 : 0.070268;0.171322;0.027288
}

# eigenes Chassis-Modell und eigene Kollision

collision_override: "/vehicle/trailer_owned/your_double/chassis_rear.pmc"

# Stuetze 0 vorne: geht immer runter, wenn der Teil abgestellt wird

trailer_brace_down_sound[0]: "/sound/your_trailer.bank#legs/down"

# Stuetze 1 hinten: beim Trennen an der Firma, sonst ab 5500 kg Ladung

# Fleet & Road Realism - Beispiel: HCT Sattelauflieger + Dolly + Sattelauflieger

def/vehicle/trailer_owned/your_trailer/chassis/your_chassis.v3def 
# Fleet & Road Realism - Auflieger-Chassisdaten (optional) / trailer chassis data (optional)
#
# Datei: gleicher Ordner und Name wie die Chassis-.sii des eigenen Aufliegers
# File:  same folder and name as the chassis .sii of the owned trailer
#        /def/vehicle/trailer_owned/your_trailer/chassis/your_chassis.sii
#        ->  your_chassis.v3def
#
# Ohne diese Datei haengen Gesamtgewicht und Sattellast von der Achszahl ab:
# 1 -> 20 t / 10 t, 2 -> 30 t / 12 t, 3 und mehr -> 39 t / 12 t, Federung air,
# registration own.
# Without this file the gross weight and the king pin load depend on the
# number of axles: 1 -> 20 t / 10 t, 2 -> 30 t / 12 t, 3 or more -> 39 t / 12 t,
# suspension air, registration own.


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Zulaessiges Gesamtgewicht des Aufliegers laut Zulassung
# Tonnen (Werte bis 100) oder Kilogramm (Werte ueber 100)
# Permissible gross vehicle weight of the trailer as registered
# Tonnes (values up to 100) or kilograms (values above 100)
#
# Wofuer: oesterreichische Kfz-Steuer, Schweizer LSVA, Schweizer kantonale
#         Motorfahrzeugsteuer (Nutzlast = dieser Wert - Leergewicht),
#         italienische IPT (Nutzlast), ungarische Kfz-Steuer (Leergewicht +
#         50 % der Nutzlast), Slowenien (je Tonne), Kroatien, Bosnien und
#         Herzegowina, Litauen, Lettland, Montenegro, Nutzlast in Serbien und
#         Nordmazedonien
# Used for:  Austrian vehicle tax, Swiss LSVA,
#            Swiss cantonal vehicle tax (payload = this value - empty weight),
#            Italian IPT (payload), Hungarian vehicle tax (empty weight + 50 % of
#            the payload), Slovenia (per tonne), Croatia, Bosnia and
#            Herzegovina, Lithuania, Latvia, Montenegro, payload in Serbia and
#            North Macedonia
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

gross_vehicle_weight: 39.00


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Last auf dem Koenigszapfen (traegt die Sattelzugmaschine) - optional, gleiche
# Einheiten. Sie wird vom Auflieger-Gewicht abgezogen, weil die Zugmaschine sie
# schon traegt:
# Load on the king pin (carried by the tractor unit) - optional, same units
# It is subtracted from the trailer weight, because the tractor already carries it:
#
#   Steuer Oesterreich / Austrian tax:   Auflieger / trailer 39 - 12 = 27 t
#   Schweizer LSVA / Swiss LSVA:         Lkw / truck 18 + Auflieger / trailer
#                                        39 - 12 = 45 t  ->  begrenzt / limited to 40 t
#
# Ausserdem: Kroatien, Bosnien und Herzegowina und Litauen (Sattelauflieger nach
# gross_vehicle_weight - king_pin_load), Sattelauflieger sind in Slowenien frei,
# eigene Tarife fuer Sattelauflieger in Montenegro, Nordmazedonien und Lettland.
# Bei Deichselanhaengern weglassen (kein Koenigszapfen).
# Also: Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Lithuania (semi-trailers by
# gross_vehicle_weight - king_pin_load), semi-trailers are free in Slovenia,
# own tariffs for semi-trailers in Montenegro, North Macedonia and Latvia.
# Leave it out for drawbar trailers (no king pin).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

king_pin_load: 12.00


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Federung der Aufliegerachsen: air (Luftfederung oder gleichwertig)
# oder leaf (jede andere Federung)
# Suspension of the trailer axles: air (air suspension or equivalent)
# or leaf (any other suspension)
#
# Wofuer: polnische, ungarische und litauische Kfz-Steuer der Auflieger
#         ("Luft" / "andere Federung")
# Used for:  Polish, Hungarian and Lithuanian vehicle tax of trailers
#            ("air" / "other suspension")
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

suspension: air


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mehrteilige Auflieger (B-Double, HCT, Drehschemelanhaenger):
#   own  = dieses Chassis ist ein eigenes Fahrzeug (Standard; auch
#          Sattelauflieger und Dollys, sie werden eigens zugelassen)
#   next = gehoert zum Teil dahinter (z. B. die Drehschemelachse eines
#          Drehschemelanhaengers)
#   prev = gehoert zum Teil davor
# Verbundene Teile sind ein Fahrzeug: eine Zulassung (Kennzeichen des hintersten
# Teils), Steuer und Versicherung einmal fuer alle. Siehe README,
# Schluessel "registration".
# Trailers made of several parts (B-double, HCT, full trailer with turntable):
#   own  = this chassis is a vehicle of its own (default; also semi-trailers
#          and converter dollies, they are registered on their own)
#   next = belongs to the part behind it (e.g. the turntable axle of a
#          full trailer)
#   prev = belongs to the part in front of it
# Joined parts are one vehicle: one registration (plate of the rearmost part),
# tax and insurance once for all of them. See README,
# key "registration".
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

registration: own


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Eigene Doubles beim Beladen trennen (Option "Eigene Doubles beim Beladen
# trennen"): welche Glieder der Kette zusammengehoeren
#   own  = dieses Glied ist eine eigene Ladeeinheit (bekommt eine eigene Spur)
#   next = bleibt beim Glied dahinter (z. B. bleibt ein Dolly unter dem
#          hinteren Sattelauflieger)
#   prev = bleibt beim Glied davor
# Jedes Chassis der Kette braucht diese Zeile; fehlt eine, wird die Kette nie
# getrennt. Ein einzelner Auflieger mit dieser Zeile wird normal beladen. Siehe
# README, Schluessel "loading".
# Splitting own doubles when loading (option "Split own doubles when loading"): which links of the chain belong together
#   own  = this link is a loading unit of its own (gets a lane of its own)
#   next = stays with the link behind it (e.g. a converter dolly stays under
#          the rear semi-trailer)
#   prev = stays with the link in front of it
# Every chassis of the chain needs this line; if one is missing, the chain is
# never split. A single trailer with this line is loaded as usual. See README,
# key "loading".
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

loading: own


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pappschilder hinten, Italien (foglio di via) und Serbien/Montenegro (PROBA):
# shift = Hoehe in mm vom Standard aus (10 mm unter dem Kennzeichen),
#         positiv = hoch, negativ = runter
# depth = vor/zurueck in mm, positiv = weg vom Fahrzeug, negativ = zum Fahrzeug
# tilt  = Grad, positiv = Oberkante zum Fahrzeug hin
# Cardboard plates at the rear, Italy (foglio di via) and Serbia/Montenegro (PROBA):
# shift = height change in mm from the default (10 mm below the plate),
#         positive = up, negative = down
# depth = forward/back in mm, positive = away from the vehicle, negative = towards
# tilt  = degrees, positive = top edge towards the vehicle
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

italy_card_shift_rear: 0
italy_card_depth_rear: 0
italy_card_tilt_rear: 0
serbia_card_shift_rear: 0
serbia_card_depth_rear: 0
serbia_card_tilt_rear: 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

docs.title: Company and container data
docs.text: Small optional files tell the mod when a company is open, whether it has a reach stacker for containers, and what a container cargo is. They work for every map and every cargo mod: the files sit next to the files the game already loads. The examples in the def/ folder of this package show the format.

docs.title: 1. Company files
docs.text:
Same folder and same name as the company files of the game, only with .v3def:

all cities    /def/company/your_company.sui
           -> /def/company/your_company.v3def

one city      /def/company/your_company/editor/your_city.sii
           -> /def/company/your_company/editor/your_city.v3def

The city file name is the city token (the editor file name up to the first dot). A city file replaces the working hours of the company file in that city, and a container_load line in a city file applies to that city only (e.g. a company that has a reach stacker at just one of its sites).

docs.title: 1a. Working hours
docs.text:
working_time :
{
monday: (06.00, 22.00)
saturday: (07.00, 12.00);(13.00, 16.00)
sunday: closed
}
  • days: monday tuesday wednesday thursday friday saturday sunday
  • one or more time spans (hh.mm, hh.mm), several separated by ;
  • 24.00 = end of the day; an end at or before the start runs past midnight, e.g. (22.00, 06.00)
  • closed = closed all day
  • a missing day = open all day
  • no file or no working_time block = the company is always open

While a company is closed, its offers are hidden, no new cargo is generated there, and its company point shows that it is closed together with the working hours.

Special transports (oversize) can have their own hours in the same file:

working_time_oversize :
{
monday: (07.00, 16.00)
saturday: closed
sunday: closed
}
  • same format as working_time
  • used for loading (start) and unloading (destination) of special transports; missing block = working_time applies
  • a special transport offer only appears if it can be loaded now, driven (50 km/h on average, at most 10 h driving per 24 h, 45 min break after 4.5 h) and unloaded in these hours before Friday 15:00 (no oversize driving Fri 15:00 - Mon 09:00)

docs.title: 1b. Reach stacker (containers)
docs.text:
container_load: truereach stacker: container cargo is given out to own container chassis, a container is lifted off on delivery container_load: falseno reach stacker: no container cargo for own container chassis, the container stays on the chassis

Companies without the line: the cargo market is not changed; on delivery the company counts as without reach stacker (container stays).

What happens with an own container chassis:

  • A container is lifted on and off only where the company has a reach stacker.
  • Delivered at a company without reach stacker, the container stays on the chassis. The chassis then works like the trailer type of the container (see 2.), with the empty weight and inner volume of the container, and the cargo market offers cargo for that trailer type.
  • Directly after unloading there, the cargo market of that company also offers "Empty container" back to one of the 10 nearest companies with reach stacker: low pay, no loading. The offer is valid as long as the truck stays on the company yard.
  • A cargo carried in the container to a company with reach stacker takes the container off the chassis.

docs.title: 1c. Cargo filters
docs.text:
Blocks with one cargo per line, written as the cargo_data name of the game (cargo.<name>, as in the cargo .sui):

ignore_in :                  cargo the company never receives
{                            (cargo market and trailer jobs)
cargo.air_mails
}
ignore_out :                 cargo the company never sends
{ ... }

freight_market: false        no cargo market offers for own trailers at this
                             company ("Cargo market" / "External cargo
                             market"); the company also never loads cargo
                             onto a trailer that is not its own
freight_market_ignore_in : { ... }    only for the cargo market
freight_market_ignore_out : { ... }

semi_trailerjob_in: false    no trailer jobs ("Freight market", trailer is
semi_trailerjob_out: false   provided) to / from this company
semi_trailerjob_ignore_in : { ... }   only for trailer jobs
semi_trailerjob_ignore_out : { ... }
  • only false is allowed for freight_market / semi_trailerjob_in / _out; a missing line = the game lists in full
  • the filters add to each other (e.g. ignore_out and semi_trailerjob_ignore_out)
  • what arrives at a company is decided only by its in folder of the game and these filters

docs.title: 1d. Trailer jobs: what happens at the destination (return trips)
docs.text:
For trailer jobs the destination company decides per body type of the trailer what happens after arrival:

semi_trailerjob_return_full :    unload, load return cargo at this company,
{                                drive back to the sender
curtainside
dryvan
}
semi_trailerjob_return_empty :   unload only; the return cargo is loaded at
{                                the nearest fitting company (same city
fueltank                         first, else outside), otherwise back empty
lowbed
}
semi_trailerjob_drop: true       pure drop yard (e.g. unaccompanied trailers
                                 for ferry or rail): every trailer is only
                                 parked, the job ends there
trailer_hub: true                transshipment point (rail or ferry
                                 terminal): as SENDER it takes back loaded
                                 trailers, the return cargo does not have to
                                 be in its in list

Body type without entry: curtainside, dryvan, refrigerated, insulated, flatbed, container, flatbed_cont = return_full; every other body type (tanks, silo, tipper, low loader, logs, livestock, car transporter ...) = return_empty. Rule of thumb: return_full for a special body only where the company loads the same body itself (quarry - tipper, sawmill - logs, car terminal - car transporter); low loaders always return_empty.

Return cargo:

  • loaded like the cargo market of the game loads a trailer that is not the company's own: the cargo must fit the trailer (body type, volume, weight), the loading company must be allowed to send it (ignore_out, freight_market rules; semi_trailerjob_out does not apply, the company only loads), the sender must accept it (its in list, ignore_in, semi_trailerjob rules) unless the sender is a trailer_hub
  • chosen at random with the cargo weights of the game, fixed per offer
  • containers: loading company with container_load: true - the container is lifted off and any container cargo goes onto the chassis; with container_load: false - the container stays, a box container is loaded with cargo of its body type, a special container (body_type = cargo name, see section 2) only with that cargo
  • the destination company never gives back the cargo it has just received
  • the whole trip is one job: one delivery time at the sender, paid at the sender: outbound + return cargo; an empty run (destination - loading company, or back empty) is paid like an empty container: 10 % of the units of the outbound cargo per km

The job list shows the trip as Start > Destination > (2nd company >) Start, the return cargo in blue after the outbound cargo, and the total distance, time and pay. A city file can hold the same lines for one city (a block in the city file goes first for its body types).

  • load = loading, unload = unloading, pickup = taking over a prepared loaded trailer, drop = parking the trailer at a pure drop yard (T)
  • minutes from-to; each check-in rolls a random time in between
  • wait_factors: factor = time spans (hh.mm or hh:mm), several spans with the same factor separated by ; an end at or before the start runs past midnight; outside all spans the factor is 1.0
  • a missing line or block uses the city file, then the company file, then the default: load/unload 30-180, pickup 5-20, drop 5-15, factors 06-10 x1.5, 16-22 x0.7, 22-06 x0.5

The waiting time sits between confirming (choosing the parking difficulty on delivery, Enter on the loading/unloading bay with an own trailer, or the loading tile) and the bay/trailer being released. On check-in a message shows the expected time. Leaving the company premises cancels the check-in. While waiting, stop on the premises and switch the engine off: a hint offers a rest until the end of the waiting time. On release everything continues by itself.

docs.title: 1f. Bays per body type (parking difficulty)
docs.text:
A company can keep bays of one difficulty free of certain body types, e.g. no low loaders at the loading docks (hard bays):

lanes_hard_ignore :          body types (body_type of the trailer, without
{                            prefix) that never load or unload on a hard bay
lowbed
lowboy
}
lanes_medium_ignore : { ... }   the same for medium bays
lanes_easy_ignore : { ... }     the same for easy bays
  • applies to every job type at this company: cargo market, driver jobs, trailer jobs and return cargo
  • loading: if the loading bay of the job is on a blocked difficulty, the job gets a free allowed loading bay of the company (fitting length, not occupied); if there is none, the bay of the game stays
  • unloading: blocked difficulties cannot be chosen
  • cargo market: if the loading company has no allowed loading bay or the destination has no allowed unloading bay for the trailer, there is no offer for it
  • the body type is the one of the trailer that is attached
  • fixed in the DLL, at every company: low loaders (lowbed, lowboy) only on easy bays; medium, hard and loading points without difficulty (e.g. docks) are always blocked for them; except trailer hubs (trailer_hub: true), where trailers are only dropped
  • a city file can hold the same blocks; they add to the company file

docs.title: 1g. Partial loads and tour planning (cargo market, own trailer)
docs.text:
A company can offer and accept partial loads in the cargo market:

units_out :                  units this company SENDS per cargo
{
default: 1-max               any amount up to a full load
cargo.furniture: 1-6         this cargo only 1 to 6 units
cargo.cement: max            this cargo only as a full load
}
units_in : { ... }           the same for what this company RECEIVES

load_mix_out :               how often a full or a partial load is offered
{                            (weights, any numbers)
default :
{
full: 60
partial: 40
}
cargo.furniture :
{
full: 20
partial: 80
}
}
load_mix_in : { ... }        the same on the receiving side
  • values: a number, from-to (e.g. 1-6), or max (= a full load)
  • a cargo.<name> line goes first, otherwise default applies
  • a city file replaces the whole block of the company file in that city
  • no units block at sender and receiver = full loads only, as in the game; a block on one side only = the other side takes full loads only
  • no load_mix block = full and partial half and half
  • tour and mixed in load_mix are reserved for a later version
  • a partial load is less than the minimum filling of the trailer (cargo_min_fill of the body type in /def/economy_trailers_data/, game default 0.8); the amount is limited to what still fits on the trailer
  • cargo with load_unit: whole (see README of the cargo data) is never offered as a partial load

Adding cargo and tour planning with partial loads:

  • "Set as GPS destination" on a cargo market offer reserves it (also before anything is loaded); taking an offer on the company yard adds it to the trip; at most 8 jobs and reservations together
  • every job and reservation takes its share of space and weight; the cargo market then only shows offers that still fit: space, weight, temperature / food / dangerous goods, delivery times, and the area: from the second cargo on, the sender AND the receiver of a new offer must each lie within 100 km (road) of a sender or receiver already in the trip (also abroad); the first cargo is free
  • a fully planned trailer locks the cargo market until a part is delivered or a reservation is cancelled
  • the active job (GPS) is the player's choice (right-click on a job tile in the main menu, or "Drive here next" in Current job), otherwise the nearest destination first unless another job would then miss its delivery time
  • the trip and the reservations are saved with the save game

body_type: <cargo name> special container made for exactly one cargo

docs.title: Icon for "Return container"

File: def/vehicle/cargo/<your_cargo_c>/accessory_container_<size>_<color>.v3def (same name as the accessory .sii, ending .v3def)

empty_icon: "/material/ui/cargo_icons/<your_icon>.mat"

The .mat must be in /material/ui/cargo_icons/ (like every cargo icon, 122 x 96 px, transparent). It is shown in the cargo market and the job info for the "Return container" offer of this container. Missing file - the mod icon for a 20 ft / 40 ft box or tank container is used.

docs.title: 3. Country file (driver wage)
docs.text:
Same folder and same name as the country file of the game, only with .v3def:

/def/country/your_country.sui
-> /def/country/your_country.v3def

driver_wage :
{
hourly_net_wage: 11.13
daily_allowance: 28
bonus_max: 25
allowance_tier[]: 8 0.5
allowance_travel[]: 0 0.5
}
  • hourly_net_wage: net wage per working hour; a driver tour pays at most 10 working hours per calendar day and 48 hours per tour (a tour lasts at most 4 days + 8 hours)
  • daily_allowance: allowance for one full day of absence
  • the tour starts when it is taken and ends with the delivery report; calendar days in game time. Full days between the first and the last day always count full. How much the first/last day and a one-day tour get depends on the country:
  • allowance_tier[]: hours share - one-day tour (start and end on the same calendar day): the share applies to MORE than these hours, the highest matching line counts; 0 = any duration. No line = nothing. allowance_tier[]: 8 0.5 (more than 8 h: half a day)
  • allowance_travel[]: hours share - first and last day of a tour over several days, hours counted on that day; missing = as allowance_tier. allowance_travel[]: 0 0.5 (always half a day)
  • allowance_meal[]: hh:mm share / night share - instead of hours: the share counts if the meal time lies within the tour on that day, night = a night spent away (not on the last day); at most 1 per day. Lines of allowance_meal replace the hour lines. allowance_meal[]: 13:00 0.333 allowance_meal[]: night 0.334
  • allowance_same_day: 0 = a one-day tour gets no allowance
  • the lines of a list replace the mod's lines for this country (all lines of that list, not single ones). Shares 0 ... 1.
  • no allowance = no allowance line in the delivery report
  • bonus_max: highest pay above the rate in percent; each start company rolls its own bonus per game week (most pay the rate), 0 = never
  • the country of the company where the tour starts decides
  • missing file or line: the mod's value for this country is used (lphd_land_v3def.zip holds them for all countries)

Driver tours (quick jobs) pay wage and allowance instead of the cargo pay. Fuel is paid by the employer (game), deductions for cargo damage or delay are taken over by the employer.

docs.title: Cargo data
docs.text: Small optional files set a surcharge per cargo and how the cargo is handled in partial loads. They sit next to the cargo files of the game.

docs.title: 1. File
docs.text:
Same folder and same name as the cargo, only with .v3def:

/def/cargo/<cargo>.v3defe.g. /def/cargo/fuel_oil.v3def

All lines are optional. Without a file the cargo behaves as in the game.

docs.title: 2. Pay
docs.text:
Freight jobs (own truck + job trailer) are paid like real traction:

  • up to 150 km 1.90 EUR/km, 150-400 km sliding, from 400 km 1.53 EUR/km
  • at least 80 EUR/h x (driving time + 1 h)
  • cargo market (own trailer) +20 %
  • urgency as delivery_window_coef in economy_data.sii

docs.title: 3. Surcharge
docs.text:
surcharge: 25percent on the freight price
  • no file or no line: no surcharge
  • empty runs get no surcharge
  • included: all ADR cargoes of the game (class 1: 30 %, classes 2 and 3: 25 %, classes 4, 6 and 8: 15 %)

docs.title: 4. Partial loads (cargo market, own trailer)
docs.text:
load_unit: palletsingle | pallet | whole
  • whole = full load only, never a partial load
  • single, pallet = partial loads allowed (piece goods or pallets)
  • no line = partial loads allowed if the companies allow them (units_out / units_in, see README_company_data)

Pay of a partial load: pallet rate (European average) by distance.

  • pallets = share of the trailer x 34
  • up to 5 pallets: 100 / 150 / 215 / 265 EUR at 100 / 350 / 650 / 1200 km
  • from 15 pallets: 70 / 105 / 150 / 190 EUR at 100 / 350 / 650 / 1200 km
  • sliding in between, rising further beyond 1200 km
  • at most the flat rate of the full load
  • urgency and surcharge apply as for the full load

Waiting time for loading and unloading: in proportion to the amount, at least 10 minutes.

docs.title: 5. Compatibility (adding cargo, tour planning)
docs.text:
temp: 2;8temperature range from;to in degrees C food: truefood

Only what fits together goes into one trailer:

  • temperature ranges must overlap (no temp line = fits everything)
  • food/feed never together with toxic cargo (ADR class 6, CV28) (ADR class from the game's cargo .sui, adr_class)
  • explosives (ADR class 1) never with other dangerous goods, allowed with normal cargo (ADR 7.5.2.1)
  • ADR classes 2 to 8 freely with each other

docs.title: 6. Cargo model, lashing and loading
docs.text:
lashing_method: directdirect | top_over lash_through: truetrue | false ramp: truetrue | false volume: 15.6volume per unit in m3 unit_volume_factor: 0.1667factor per cargo model
  • lashing_method: lashing method of the cargo (direct = direct lashing at the cargo, top_over = tie-down over the cargo). Replaces the method of the cargo_model_match files of the cargo.
  • lash_through: true = the strap runs through the cargo (when securing by hand), e.g. for pipes or coils.
  • ramp: true = the cargo goes onto the trailer over the ramp (self-driving or rollable). In mixed loads only on low-bed trailers, never with a gooseneck.
  • volume: replaces the volume per unit of the game's cargo definition.
  • unit_volume_factor: replaces the factor of the cargo_model_match. Below 1 means: one cargo model is 1 / factor units (0.1667 = 6 units). Partial loads then come only in whole cargo models.

docs.text:
key: value
  • one entry per line, spaces around the colon are allowed
  • lines starting with # or // are comments, a # after the value too
  • numbers with decimal point, no units on the line
  • a line with a wrong value is reported in game.log and ignored

docs.title: Cargo securing
docs.text: Small optional files tell the mod how a cargo is secured and how it behaves: edge guards, wear at edges, tipping and sliding, anti-slip mats, deck and your own lashing gear. They work for every cargo mod: the files sit next to the files the game already loads. The examples in the def/ folder of this package show the format. Everything works with the option "secure cargo yourself"; anti-slip mats are laid by the mod itself without the option.

docs.title: 1. Cargo model (cargo_model_match)
docs.text:
Same folder and same name as the cargo_model_match file of the cargo, only with .v3def:

/def/vehicle/cargo/your_cargo/model_area.sii
-> /def/vehicle/cargo/your_cargo/model_area.v3def

If there are several match files (e.g. model_area.sii and model_area_1.sii), each one gets its own .v3def. All entries are optional; without the file the defaults apply. An entry with a wrong format is listed as an error in the log (file and value read), that line is then not used.

docs.title: 1a. Edge guards
docs.text: edge_guard: trueguards can be placed when securing by hand (default: false) edge_guard_width: 0.20width of the guard in m, 0.01 - 2 (default: strap = strap width + 0.20, threaded + 0.04; chain 0.20) edge_guard_leg: 0.10leg length on each side of the edge in m, 0.005 - 1 (default: strap 0.10, threaded 0.05; chain 0.15)

docs.title: 1b. Wear at edges
docs.text: edge_wear: 0.4wear of the strap at an edge without guard, 0.0 - 1.0 (default 0.5). With a guard only a fifth counts. Together with the give of the ratchet the strap becomes loose (from 75 %). edge_crush: 0.5crushing of the cargo at an edge without guard, 0.0 - 1.0 (default 0.5) - for a later version, no effect yet.

docs.title: 1c. Tipping of loose cargo
docs.text:
If a lashing on a cargo piece is loose, the piece can tip in corners and when braking - as far as the loose lashing lets it - and drops back with an impact. A tight lashing on the piece holds it. All values in model coordinates (m): x across, y up, z along.

tilt[]: falsethis cargo model never tips (e.g. very flat or firmly chocked cargo). Default: true. 
tilt_base[]: "single|(x, z)|radius"
    One support point (wheel, foot, prop). Radius = half tyre or foot
    width, the contact reaches that far outwards (optional, default 0).
tilt_base[]: "area|(x, z)|(x, z)"
    A support area: outer dimensions as two opposite corners
    (crate, pallet, frame, chocks).
tilt_base[]: "ring|(x, z)|outer radius|inner radius|angle from|angle to"
    A ring or ring segment (upright pipe section, formwork, arch):
    circle centre, outer and inner radius, arc from - to in degrees
    (0 = towards +x, 90 = towards +z). Without angles: full ring.
    Example half ring over -x: "ring|(1.53, 0.0)|3.05|2.40|90|270"

Several lines and all types can be mixed; the support area is the outline around all points. The piece tips about its edge. Without tilt_base[] the mod uses the lowest points of the model (mesh).

Material or friction value (optional, first field of each tilt_base line):
what the support area is made of. This gives the static friction on the
deck (for sliding) and whether an anti-slip mat is needed there
(section 3). Default 0.45.
    "material|single|(x, z)|radius"
    "material|area|(x, z)|(x, z)"
    "material|ring|(x, z)|outer radius|inner radius|angle from|angle to"
Materials (value on a wooden deck):
    wood 0.50       sawn wood (beams, crates, skids)
    plastic 0.20    plastic
    metal 0.45      steel / metal
    concrete 0.55   concrete
    rubber 0.60     rubber (tyres, rubber tracks)
    straw 0.40      straw
Instead of a material a number 0.01 - 1.5 works too (friction on a wooden
deck). Guide values per EN 12195-1: planed wood 0.3, rough concrete 0.7.
The value is combined with the deck of the trailer (section 4).
Example wheel: tilt_base[]: "rubber|single|(-0.75, -0.40)|0.08"
Example skid: tilt_base[]: "wood|area|(-1.15, -0.70)|(1.15, -0.60)"

coll_base[]: "single|(x, y, z)|radius"
coll_base[]: "area|(x, y, z)|(x, y, z)"
coll_base[]: "cylinder|(x, y, z)|(x, y, z)|radius"
    parts that touch the deck when tipping (forks, bucket, attachment,
    overhang). Tipping stops there. single = point with radius,
    area = surface from two opposite corners (x, y, z). Height and width
    change evenly along the length (z): different heights = sloped. If the
    corners are left and right of the centre, the surface is a trapezoid
    symmetric to the centre (+-x at each end, e.g. wide and low at the
    fender, narrow and higher at the end of the box). If both are on the
    same side, it is a rectangle between them (e.g. mast beside the centre).
    cylinder = cylinder (boiler, pipe): centre of both end faces (start and
    end point) and radius. A second radius after it applies at the end point
    (cone, transition): "cylinder|(x, y, z)|(x, y, z)|1.70|0.80"
    Without entry the mod uses all model points up to 0.6 m height.
tilt_cog[]: (x, y, z)centre of gravity. Without entry: centre of the model. Low and far inside = stable, high and close to an edge = tips early. 
sounds[]: "drop|/sound/your_mod/your.bank#your_event"
    sound when dropping back (FMOD event, one-shot, parameters impact 0-1 =
    hardness of the impact, mass 0-1 = weight / 20 t, aero_wnd 0-2 = cabin
    closed/open). "drop|-" = no sound. Without entry:
    /sound/lphd/lashing.bank#cargo_drop. .soundref is possible too.

Several models in one match (several data_path[]):
Without a number, tilt[], tilt_base[], coll_base[], tilt_cog[] and sounds[] apply to
models of the match. With a number only to the model at that position in
data_path[] (first = 0):
  tilt_base[0]: "area|(-1.08, -1.50)|(1.08, 5.80)"
  tilt_cog[0]: (0.00, 1.35, 1.80)
  sounds[0]: "drop|/sound/lphd/lashing.bank#cargo_drop"
  tilt[1]: false
tilt[], tilt_cog[] and sounds[] with a number replace the value without.
tilt_base and coll_base with a number are added: all lines without a
number and all with the model's number apply together.

docs.title: 2. Lashing gear
docs.text:
Own file in the folder /def/vehicle, name starts with lashing_gear_data:

/def/vehicle/lashing_gear_data.your_mod.v3def

In square brackets the name of the cargo_lashing_gear unit from the lashing_gear_data file of the game or the mod (e.g. .strap, .chain).

loosen_minutes[.your_strap]: 10
    minutes of hard driving (summed, e.g. corners with about 4 m/s2
    lateral) until the lashing loosens. Without entry: strap 10, chain 20.
    Added per lashing: a spread, the position on the cargo piece, the
    weight per lashing, the free length and the angle.

lashing_capacity[.your_strap]: 2.5
    lashing capacity LC in t (label in daN / 1000, e.g. LC 2500 daN
    = 2.5). The more the lashing is loaded (weight per lashing / LC),
    the faster it loosens. Without entry: strap 2.5, chain 6.3.

sounds[.your_strap]: "loose|/sound/your_mod/your.bank#your_event"
    sound of the loose lashing (middle of the strap), loop with the
    parameters aero_speed 0-200, aero_wnd 0-2, slack 0-1.
sounds[.your_strap]: "rattle|/sound/your_mod/your.bank#your_event"
    rattling ratchet or tensioner, same parameters.

"-" instead of a path = no sound. Several equal names: the straps take turns. Without entry: strap strap_noise + ratchet_rattle, chain chain_noise (no separate rattle), all from /sound/lphd/lashing.bank.

docs.title: 3. Anti-slip mats
docs.text:
For each support area from tilt_base[] the mod calculates: value of the material x factor of the deck at that spot (section 4). Below 0.60 the area gets an anti-slip mat. Without tilt_base[] there are no mats.

  • With "secure cargo yourself" the player lays the mats before loading in a separate scene (marker at each area). Without the option, on pre-loaded job trailers and on parked trailers the mod lays them itself.
  • Mat: 8 mm thick, friction 0.60 regardless of cargo and deck. The cargo stands with its underside on the mat; if only some areas have mats, it rests tilted on the mat edge.
  • Size: small area (both sides up to 0.5 m) completely; larger area pieces of 0.3 m at the corners and every 1.2 m along the edges; single as a square (radius up to 0.25 m) or pieces on the circle; ring pieces on the middle radius every 1.2 m.
  • Mats are cut off at the edge of the deck. Pieces under 2 cm are left out - single needs a radius of at least 0.01 for that.

Tip: tyres and rubber tracks (rubber) need no mat, wooden skids and steel on wood do, on a metal deck almost everything does.

docs.title: 4. Deck (trailer)
docs.text:
Own file next to the body file of the trailer, same name with .v3def (without a body next to the chassis file):

/def/vehicle/trailer_owned/your_trailer/body/your_body.sii
-> /def/vehicle/trailer_owned/your_trailer/body/your_body.v3def

floor: wood               deck: wood (factor 1.00), metal (0.70) or film
                          (film-faced plywood, 0.60). Default: wood.
floor[]: "metal|x1|x2"    strip with a different deck over the full length,
                          from x1 to x2 across in m (trailer coordinates,
                          0 = centre). Several lines possible, e.g. steel
                          frame outside and wood in between.

The factor is multiplied with the value of the material of the support area (sliding and anti-slip mats).

docs.title: 5. Models of the lashing gear (hook, ratchet, tensioner)
docs.text:
So that hook and ratchet sit correctly when securing, the model gets a file next to its .pmd, same name with .v3def. These are the models named in the lashing_gear_data (hook at the start, hook at the end, ratchet or tensioner):

/vehicle/your_mod/lashing/your_hook.pmd
-> /vehicle/your_mod/lashing/your_hook.v3def

Hook:

lphd_lash_model : .hook {
    pivot: (0.0, 0.0, -0.025)     pivot: the point with which the hook hangs
                                  in the eye or at the lashing point
    tip: (0.0, -0.04, -0.03)      tip (read, currently without effect)
    sounds[]: "hook|/sound/your_mod/your.bank#hook"
}

Ratchet / tensioner:

lphd_lash_model : .binder {
    in: (0.0, 0.0, 0.085)         shaft the strap or chain runs onto
    fixed: (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)        bolt the ratchet hangs on
    contact: (0.0, -0.018, 0.042) contact: this side rests against the
                                  vehicle or the cargo (without entry:
                                  the same all round, e.g. chain tensioner)
    lever: (0.0, 0.045, -0.092)   end of the lever (tensioning)
    sounds[]: "ratchet_up|/sound/your_mod/your.bank#ratchet_up"
}
  • points in metres in the space of the model, written as (x, y, z)
  • without a file or without points the model lies as the game sets it
  • a ratchet needs in and fixed, otherwise it counts as without points

Sounds (sounds[]: "name|path", path to a .soundref or bank#event, "-" = no sound, several equal names: one of them at random). Without entry it is silent.

hookhook_in hooking in (otherwise hook) hook_out unhooking (otherwise hook) strap_throw / chain_throw throwing the strap or chain over, at the end hook (otherwise throw) ratchetratchet_up lever up ratchet_down lever down, tensioning (otherwise tension) ratchet_open opening (otherwise ratchet_up)
